Iam.//: Tenants to ensure exist at startup. A realm no tenant row claims is not a trusted issuer, so without these the dev realms the AppHost imports would authenticate nobody. Each Id MUST match the hardcoded `tenant` claim in the matching realm file — they are two halves of one fact. Replaced by tenant provisioning (IAM-10).

SeedTenants.Name: Veridian Beverages (dev)
SeedTenants.//Users: Each SubjectId MUST match the pinned `id` of that user in the realm file. Keycloak generates a subject on import and the dev Keycloak has no data volume, so before those ids were pinned every restart produced a different subject — orphaning the previous run's rows and making this impossible.

Org.//: Puts the seeded rep on a territory, which is what a device pull is scoped by (BR-ORG-3). Without it a rep signs in to an empty app — no shops, no round, nothing to order against. The territory is matched by name and never created: on a fresh database there are no territories or outlets to cover, and this logs that it found none rather than inventing an empty one.

Journey.//: Publishes a round covering today, so the field app has a day to work. Both regression sweeps asked for this: a rep with no published round cannot reach check-in, the audit or order capture, so a manual pass gets no further than the empty-round message. It runs the real generator — setting a per-shop frequency and a working week first — rather than writing calls into the table, because a seeder that skipped generation would leave a break in JRN-03 invisible to every browser pass.
Journey.//idempotence: By coverage of *today*, not by row existence: a dev environment left running drifts out of any fixed window, and a round that went stale three weeks ago is the same empty app. Restarting re-seeds when today is uncovered.
